name: Bemiparin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Bemiparin is a low-molecular-weight heparin whose anti-Xa exposure is significantly higher at creatinine clearance (CrCl) below 30 mL/min. The Spanish label needs no change at CrCl 30–80 (with clinical monitoring) and reduces the treatment dose to 75% (about 85 IU/kg once daily) below 30, with anti-Xa monitoring. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: Spanish summary of product characteristics (ficha técnica) uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min).

bands.recommendation: Treatment of DVT: 115 IU anti-Xa/kg SC once daily for 7 ± 2 days (weight bands 5,000 to 12,500 IU) (ficha técnica).
CrCl 30–80: no dose adjustment; careful clinical monitoring (ficha técnica).

CrCl <30: exposure rises. After weighing bleeding and thrombosis risk, use 75% of the treatment dose (about 85 IU anti-Xa/kg once daily) in acute DVT; monitor closely and consider anti-Xa about 4 hours after a dose (ficha técnica).

CrCl <30: exposure rises. After weighing bleeding and thrombosis risk, use 75% of the treatment dose (about 85 IU anti-Xa/kg once daily) in acute DVT; monitor closely and consider anti-Xa about 4 hours after a dose (ficha técnica). No data below CrCl 15; unfractionated heparin is generally preferred.

hd.text: Not studied (no hemodialysis-circuit or treatment dose for dialysis in the ficha técnica). Avoid; unfractionated heparin is preferred, with specialist input.

pd.text: Not addressed; if used, as CrCl <30 with anti-Xa monitoring.

monitoring: Platelets on day 1, every 3 to 4 days and at the end of treatment (heparin-induced thrombocytopenia). Potassium before and during treatment in at-risk patients (kidney failure, diabetes), especially beyond 7 days. Anti-Xa at CrCl <30. Neuraxial anesthesia timing (ficha técnica 4.4).
